papers.title: Trajectory-Optimized Sensing for Active Search of Tissue Abnormalities in Robotic Surgery
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop an approach for guiding robots to automatically localize and find the shapes of tumors and other stiff inclusions present in the anatomy. Our approach uses Gaussian processes to model the stiffness distribution and active learning to direct the palpation path of the robot. The palpation paths are chosen such that they maximize an acquisition function provided by an active learning algorithm. Our approach provides the flexibility to avoid obstacles in the robot's path, incorporate uncertainties in robot position and sensor measurements, include prior information about location of stiff inclusions while respecting the robot-kinematics. To the best of our knowledge this is the first work in literature that considers all the above conditions while localizing tumors. The proposed framework is evaluated via simulation and experimentation on three different robot platforms: 6-DoF industrial arm, da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK), and the Insertable Robotic Effector Platform (IREP). Results show that our approach can accurately estimate the locations and boundaries of the stiff inclusions while reducing exploration time.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法使用高斯过程作为代理模型，但应用于机器人触诊，与生物力学有限元代理建模无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: Paper does not address FEA simulation efficiency, constrained optimization, or implant/biomechanics design; it focuses on active sensing for tumor localization in surgery.

summary_zh.motivation: 自动化手术中肿瘤定位与形状识别
summary_zh.method: 使用高斯过程建模刚度分布，主动学习引导触诊路径
summary_zh.result: 准确估计肿瘤位置与边界，减少探索时间
summary_zh.validation: 在三种机器人平台上进行仿真与实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To automatically localize and determine the shapes of stiff inclusions such as tumors during robotic surgery.
summary_en.method: Gaussian processes model the stiffness distribution and active learning selects palpation paths that maximize an acquisition function.
summary_en.result: The proposed approach accurately estimates locations and boundaries of stiff inclusions while reducing exploration time.
summary_en.validation: Validation performed via simulation and experimentation on three different robotic platforms: a 6-DoF arm, dVRK, and IREP.

papers.title: Decentralized High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization with Factor Graphs
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel decentralized high-dimensional Bayesian optimization (DEC-HBO) algorithm that, in contrast to existing HBO algorithms, can exploit the interdependent effects of various input components on the output of the unknown objective function f for boosting the BO performance and still preserve scalability in the number of input dimensions without requiring prior knowledge or the existence of a low (effective) dimension of the input space. To realize this, we propose a sparse yet rich factor graph representation of f to be exploited for designing an acquisition function that can be similarly represented by a sparse factor graph and hence be efficiently optimized in a decentralized manner using distributed message passing. Despite richly characterizing the interdependent effects of the input components on the output of f with a factor graph, DEC-HBO can still guarantee no-regret performance asymptotically. Empirical evaluation on synthetic and real-world experiments (e.g., sparse Gaussian process model with 1811 hyperparameters) shows that DEC-HBO outperforms the state-of-the-art HBO algorithms.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法通过因子图分解实现高维贝叶斯优化，可转移至FEA代理模型的采样效率优化，但未直接应用于生物力学或植入物设计。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not apply the method to FEA or biomechanics design scenarios nor handles constraints explicitly.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决高维贝叶斯优化在输入维度高时的可扩展性问题
summary_zh.method: 利用因子图分解目标函数并设计基于消息传递的分布式采集函数优化
summary_zh.result: 在合成和真实高维问题上优于现有方法
summary_zh.validation: 通过合成函数和稀疏高斯过程超参数优化实验验证

summary_en.motivation: Address scalability challenges in high-dimensional Bayesian optimization without assuming low effective dimensionality.
summary_en.method: Proposes a factor graph decomposition of the objective function that enables decentralized optimization of a sparsely represented acquisition function via message passing.
summary_en.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art high-dimensional BO methods on synthetic and real-world tasks including tuning 1811 hyperparameters.
summary_en.validation: Validated through synthetic objective functions and a sparse Gaussian process hyperparameter tuning problem.

papers.title: Sequential Randomized Matrix Factorization for Gaussian Processes: Efficient Predictions and Hyper-parameter Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper presents a sequential randomized lowrank matrix factorization approach for incrementally predicting values of an unknown function at test points using the Gaussian Processes framework. It is well-known that in the Gaussian processes framework, the computational bottlenecks are the inversion of the (regularized) kernel matrix and the computation of the hyper-parameters defining the kernel. The main contributions of this paper are two-fold. First, we formalize an approach to compute the inverse of the kernel matrix using randomized matrix factorization algorithms in a streaming scenario, i.e., data is generated incrementally over time. The metrics of accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed method are compared against a batch approach based on use of randomized matrix factorization and an existing streaming approach based on approximating the Gaussian process by a finite set of basis vectors. Second, we extend the sequential factorization approach to a class of kernel functions for which the hyperparameters can be efficiently optimized. All results are demonstrated on two publicly available datasets.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法可加速高斯过程代理模型的计算，但未涉及约束处理、不确定性量化或在植入物设计中的验证。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA surrogate modeling, constraint handling, or biomechanical design applications, and validation is limited to benchmark datasets.

summary_zh.motivation: 降低高斯过程预测和超参数优化的计算成本。
summary_zh.method: 提出顺序随机低秩矩阵分解方法，增量式更新核矩阵逆。
summary_zh.result: 在精度相近下，计算效率优于批次方法和现有流式方法。
summary_zh.validation: 在公开数据集上比较精度与计算时间。

summary_en.motivation: To reduce the computational bottleneck of Gaussian process inference and hyperparameter optimization in streaming scenarios.
summary_en.method: A sequential randomized low-rank matrix factorization approach is proposed to incrementally update the inverse of the regularized kernel matrix.
summary_en.result: The method achieves competitive accuracy with significantly lower computational cost compared to batch and existing streaming approaches.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on two publicly available datasets, measuring prediction accuracy and runtime.
